goal: Decide whether a WASM-GEMM-GNAF document may call a claim proved, a theorem or globally optimal, so no README or ledger row says more than the Lean kernel checked.

app.name: gnaf-claim-wording
app.title: GNAF claim wording
app.purpose: Decide whether a strong word may be used for a claim row, from its claim level, its declaration, its axioms and its scope.

fields.name: word
fields.means: the word a document wants to use for the claim

fields.name: level
fields.means: the claim level of the row in model/claims.json

fields.name: declaration
fields.means: whether the Lean declaration the row names exists in the compiled environment

fields.name: axioms
fields.means: the transitive axioms the declaration reaches

fields.name: scope
fields.means: whether the declaration is the release-scoped statement or a generic or conditional lemma

meanings.permit: XACML 3.0 section 7: Permit; the document may use the word for this claim
meanings.deny: XACML 3.0 section 7: Deny; the word overstates what the claim establishes
meanings.not-applicable: XACML 3.0 section 7: NotApplicable; the strong-wording policy does not govern this word
meanings.indeterminate: XACML 3.0 section 7: Indeterminate; the declaration cannot be found, so the policy cannot be evaluated

rules.why: SPEC.md 17.1 restricts only proved, theorem and globally optimal; a measurement is reported, not promoted
SPEC.md 17.1: an external citation is an authority row and uses its own words
SPEC.md 17.1: only formalProof supports proved, theorem or globally optimal; tests, benchmarks, citations and measurements cannot promote a claim
SPEC.md 17.2: the conformance tool must confirm the declaration exists in the compiled Lean environment before the row is credited
README.md: what is proved is kernel-checked and sorry-free
README.md: declarations reaching Classical.choice as executable witnesses are recorded as uncredited, not counted as formal proof
WasmGemmGnaf/Theorems/Status.lean: the generic argmin and other conditional infrastructure do not instantiate the release claim

app.otherwiseWhy: a formal-proof row whose declaration exists, reaches only propext, Quot.sound and Prop-level Classical.choice, and is used at its own scope

properties.why: SPEC.md 17.1: nothing short of formalProof supports a strong word
README.md: the generic finite-argmin lemma does not identify a committed artifact
README.md: executable Classical.choice witnesses are uncredited
a measured number is reported with its corpus, never worded as a proof

stakeholders.name: Release reviewer
stakeholders.text: Reviews README.md, CERTIFICATION.md and CONFORMANCE.md and needs no sentence to claim global optimality before the release theorem closes.

stakeholders.name: Maintainer
stakeholders.text: Adds claim rows and prose and needs to know, row by row, which words the row supports.

concerns.name: Honest wording
concerns.text: A strong word appears only beside a formal-proof row whose declaration the kernel checked at its own scope.

components.name: Lean 4 kernel
components.text: Lean 4.30.0, which checks every declaration and reports its transitive axioms.

components.name: UOR-GNAF authority
components.text: The pinned UOR-GNAF authority whose total answer carrier fixes the terminal answer WorkloadIncomplete.

components.name: Conformance tool
components.text: The xtask gate that loads the compiled environment, recomputes identities and enforces the dependency firewall.

threats.name: Benchmark promoted to proof
threats.text: A benchmark or test result is worded as proved or globally optimal.

control.name: Formal proof only
control.text: Only a formal-proof row is permitted a strong word.

threats.name: Generic lemma cited as release theorem
threats.text: Universal.exists_globalOptimal_of_nonempty is cited as if it were the release-scoped optimality theorem.

control.name: Scope check
control.text: Global optimality is denied for any conditional declaration.

threats.name: Self-recorded proposition
threats.text: A row records GlobalOptimal := True so its hash matches itself.

control.name: Dependency firewall
control.text: The conformance tool unfolds scope-critical definitions and compares them to the WGG-GO-1 authority schema.

quality.text: No strong word is permitted for a row below formal proof or with uncredited axioms.
quality.measureText: Requests below formal proof or with executable-choice or sorry axioms that answer permit.

quality.text: A permit always names a declaration the compiled environment holds.
quality.measureText: Requests with an absent declaration that answer permit.
